ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under FINTRAC rules against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian autonomous sanctions promulgated under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), the Criminal Code terrorist entity listings, and, as a prudent cross-border compliance measure for USD wire settlements, the U.S. OFAC SDN and sectoral/ownership 50% lists. Each general partner, limited partner, beneficial owner, and authorized signatory must be screened before registration, at renewal, and upon any material event. statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises (REQ) online portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, the declared business name must be in French; an English or other-language version may be registered concurrently only where the French name is the primary name. A Quebec societé en commandite must include a legal designation: 'société en commandite' or 's.e.c.' in French, and 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' where the English designation has been approved. Names must be written in Latin characters; non-Latin script names require an official transliteration approved by the Registrar, and the transliterated name must be accompanied by a French-language rendering. The name must be distinctive, cannot be exclusively generic or descriptive, must not contain obscene or scandalous matter, and must not suggest a public institution or regulated activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 90 days and is not extendable; if it lapses, a new reservation must be submitted before refiling. If the Registrar refuses a name, the applicant may (1) request written reasons; (2) file a revised reservation incorporating a new distinctive element, with a French-language explanation of the change; (3) submit an administrative review application to the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal; and (4) if the administrative review fails, bring a judicial appeal to the Court of Québec under the review provisions of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises within the applicable statutory delay. Legal counsel should accompany the administrative appeal with a certified French translation and an official name-search report.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a non-regulated 3D art and game-asset outsourcing service entity. The limited partnership must maintain a Quebec registered establishment address that is a real and accessible place of business or service address, capable of receiving legal process and accommodating inspection of registers. A serviced executive suite or professional registered-agent address is acceptable; a bare post-office box is not sufficient. No physical retail presence, commercial premises floor area, or industry-specific license is required for this ISIC 7490 creative BPO activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. For an unlicensed creative-BPO limited partnership with no cash-intensive operations and no regulated activity, the annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Registraire, Revenu Québec, or FINTRAC examination team is approximately 1% to 3%. The probability increases to approximately 5% to 10% if atypical large wire transfers, nominee-flagged ownership, sanctions/PEP red flags, or repeated UBO disclosure deficiencies appear.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Corporate Name Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (online name reservation service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the enterprise registrar's online portal, selecting the legal form 'Société en commandite' (Limited Partnership). Verify the proposed corporate name against the Quebec enterprise register and common-law trademarks.
required_dossiers: Proposed name in French and/or English
Description of the partnership's principal business activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected due to similarity, file an application for review with the registrar, provide a reasoned legal distinction, or submit a revised name reservation with a new proposed name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting the Declaration of Registration and Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or authorized legal counsel in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Declaration of Registration in compliance with Quebec's legal publicity regime and prepare a written Limited Partnership Agreement. The declaration must identify the general partner, limited partners, registered office, and the restricted activities of limited partners.
required_dossiers: Identity and contact details of all partners and the general partner
Statutory declaration of the general partner
Certificate of address or proof of registered office location
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registrar requests amendments, revise the declaration and re-file promptly, ensuring that the limited partner does not participate in management to preserve limited liability.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Registration with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (online filing platform)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Declaration of Registration electronically via the registraire's portal or filed in paper form with the required attestation of the general partner. Pay the statutory registration fee and obtain the Quebec Enterprise Registration Number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of filing fee
Authorization of the general partner for filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is queried or rejected, review the registrar's notice, correct deficiencies such as address or partner information, and resubmit within 30 days; any late filing may incur late submission charges.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance and Opening of Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Lead financial institution (schedule I chartered bank or credit union in Quebec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt governance resolutions covering authorization of the general partner to manage the partnership, open corporate bank accounts, execute contracts, and appoint officers. Present the NEQ certificate and partnership agreement to the banking institution for account opening.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Limited Partnership Agreement
Board or general partner resolution authorizing banking signatories
Proof of identity and address of the general partner and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening due to documentation insufficiency, obtain certified translations or notarized certifications and provide a revised Organizational and Resolutions Summary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations and Revenu Québec Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (in collaboration with the Canada Revenue Agency)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for Quebec provincial tax accounts, including QST, if applicable, and obtain the employer account for source deductions if hiring staff. Provide the NEQ and confirm the partnership's pass-through tax status with each partner's tax number.
required_dossiers: List of partners and their Canadian tax identifiers
Declaration of business type and estimated annual revenue
Banking confirmation of the partnership account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed due to missing partner information, supply completed T183 partnership return information and coordinate with the general partner's tax advisor to accelerate the registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal direct tax and GST/HST administration; Revenu Québec (RQ) — provincial QST and income tax administration. Electronic client portals: CRA My Business Account (www.canada.ca/cra-business-account) and RQ Online Services for Businesses / CLIC (www.revenuquebec.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File the Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) declaration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) before commencing activity. Step 2: Register the partnership with CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) — online via 'Register a business with the CRA' or Form RC1 — and open the GST/HST account (and, if applicable, payroll and import/export accounts). Step 3: Complete the QST registration with Revenu Québec (generally integrated through the NEQ and BN); non-resident registrants without a Canadian establishment must appoint a GST/HST/QST representative under section 305 ETA and file using CRA's International Tax Services Office procedures (Form RC104 for non-resident accounts). Step 4: Activate CRA 'My Business Account' and RQ 'CLIC' credentials for portal filing and direct-debit remittance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the Canadian/Quebec limited partnership is a fiscally transparent flow-through entity; the LP itself is not subject to federal or provincial income tax. Each partner (including non-resident limited partners) is taxed on its share of income as earned; the partnership is treated as a separate registrant/person for GST/HST and QST purposes to the extent it carries on a commercial activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box or elective entity classification regime; flow-through treatment is statutory and mandatory. Practical statutory elections affecting the LP and its non-resident partners include: (i) the subsection 216(1) ITA election permitting a non-resident to file a Canadian income tax return on net rental/business income, (ii) elections to treat Canada–U.S. or other treaty partners' hybrid entities consistently under Canada's OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch rules, and (iii) GST/HST elections such as the 'single joint election' for parties to a joint venture (where relevant).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under the Excise Tax Act (federal, 5% in Quebec) plus QST/TVQ (Québec Sales Tax) under the Act respecting the Québec sales tax — both administered in Quebec by Revenu Québec; no separate provincial sales tax applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 — mandatory GST/HST and QST registration where the taxable supply threshold (taxable supplies made in Canada / in Quebec in either a single calendar quarter or the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters) exceeds C$30,000; non-residents making taxable supplies in Canada through a Canadian establishment, or supplying real property situated in Canada, are generally required to register without regard to the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based continuous transaction control or digital stamping regime exists in Canada. CRA and Revenu Québec support Peppol-based e-invoicing (BIS 3.0) on an opt-in basis; paper and PDF invoices remain valid. Mandatory electronic obligations: GST/HST registrants with annual revenue over C$1.5 million must file returns electronically and remit funds electronically when net tax payable exceeds C$10,000; exporters must file advance customs declarations through CBSA ACI/eManifest.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Registered suppliers may zero-rate export supplies of 3D game art, sculpting and rigging services where the recipient is a non-resident person, the service is not performed in relation to real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance, and the digital deliverables are supplied for use wholly outside Canada. Physical goods exported directly to a non-resident are zero-rated when shipped out of Canada and supported by prescribed export evidence. Pure electronic delivery of game assets does not require customs clearance, but the supplier must retain contract, non-resident identity, delivery and payment documents to substantiate the zero-rating claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A or CBSA ACI eManifest) — required where tangible goods ship across the border; not applicable to pure digital services
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing shipment to a named foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate — SWIFT MT103 / bank foreign-exchange conversion record evidencing receipt of foreign currency export consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Without adequate export evidence, CRA/Revenu Québec will reassess the zero-rated supply as taxable, recapture related input tax credits, and assess arrears interest plus penalties (ETA s.280; AQRT equivalent). False statements, neglect or misrepresentation on returns invoke a gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the tax at issue; wilful evasion is criminally prosecutable with fines up to C$100,000 (indictment) and imprisonment, and the normal four-year reassessment period extends to ten years. For limited partnerships, general partners are jointly and severally liable for partnership GST/HST debt; limited partners who participate in the control or management may forfeit limited-liability protection.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the sole monetary authority and note-issuing central bank. Canada has no dedicated foreign exchange control agency equivalent to a SAFE-style administration; FX policy is liberalized and administered through prudential supervision by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), AML/CFT supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), and trade/sanctions enforcement by Global Affairs Canada (formerly Foreign Affairs and International Trade Canada). Retail and corporate FX dealing is additionally regulated at the provincial level in Quebec by the Autorite des marches financiers (AMF) where a money-services business is involved.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations and maintains full and unrestricted convertibility on both current-account and capital-account transactions. No exchange control licence, prior approval, or repatriation consent is required for inbound capital contributions, outbound trade settlements, or profit distributions by a Quebec societe en commandite (limited partnership). Profit remittance mechanics: because the LP is tax-transparent, distributions to non-resident partners are not dividends and are therefore not subject to the Part XIII 25% withholding tax that applies to dividends, interest, royalties, rents, or management fees. Instead, each non-resident partner is taxable under Part I on its allocable share of the partnership's Canadian-source business income, and the partnership is required to file a prescribed non-resident partner return and to remit the associated tax (the section 194 regime of the Income Tax Act); failure to remit creates joint and several liability for the partnership. A further remittance hurdle arises only on disposition of a partnership interest if the interest constitutes taxable Canadian property, in which case a purchaser-side clearance certificate under section 116 may be required; for a game-art studio holding largely working capital, receivables, and goodwill, the interest will typically not be taxable Canadian property. In practice, the only structural hurdle is the LP's obligation to register with Revenu Quebec and the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, and to provide CRA/Revenu Quebec with partner-level allocation schedules (T5013/RL-15 equivalents).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. The LP may retain USD/EUR receivables offshore or in a domestic USD account, and may convert at the time of its choosing. Reporting obligations are limited to: (i) a FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFTR) for international electronic transfers of CAD 10,000 or more in a single transaction; (ii) a FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction Report (LCTR) for cash receipts exceeding CAD 10,000; (iii) cross-border currency/ monetary instrument reporting to the CBSA for physical movement of currency exceeding CAD 10,000; and (iv) ordinary accounting translation of FX gains/losses to partners under IFRS/ASP for tax purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Foreign-incorporated digital EMI/neo-bank platforms (Wise Business, Payoneer, Airwallex, Ebury, Mercury) can be used as supplementary treasury rails but are not a substitute for a Canadian Schedule I bank account. Legally, an EMI that solicits or accepts Canadian clients must either be a registered Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC, hold an authorization or be an agent/partner of a Canadian chartered bank, and comply with Quebec AMF money-services rules where applicable. For a Canadian LP, the prudent structure is: (i) a primary corporate account at National Bank of Canada or Desjardins for CAD liquidity, statutory payments, and tax-compliance evidence; (ii) a Wise Business or Payoneer account used strictly for collecting small-balance PayPal/aggregator receivables and for low-value cross-border vendor disbursements; and (iii) a standing instruction that any EFT over CAD 10,000 must clear through SWIFT on the primary bank rail to preserve the audit trail and FINTRAC EFTR compliance. The LP's partnership agreement should expressly authorize the use of EMIs and prohibit commingling of partner funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandatory under FINTRAC rules; remote onboarding is permissible where the bank performs dual-verification KYC, such as a certified/notarized passport copy plus a second identity document or a live video interview. However, for a Quebec LP with non-resident partners or non-resident signatories, most Schedule I banks will either request an in-person meeting at a Montreal branch or require a notarized identity verification executed in the partner's country of residence. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is triggered where the general partner is a foreign corporation or where beneficial owners hold more than 25% without a Canadian SIN, ITN, or credit history. The practical recommendation: appoint a Canadian-resident general partner or a Quebec-licensed agent for service and arrange a single in-person signatory visit to National Bank or Desjardins; this reduces onboarding cycle time from 4-8 weeks to 1-2 weeks and materially increases the likelihood of a High onboarding viability outcome.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident individual beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the LP without Canadian tax identification (no SIN or ITN) and without domestic credit history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) registration extract from the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec evidencing the societe en commandite; (2) full executed partnership agreement and certificate of LP registration; (3) notarized certified true copies of passports for all general partners and 25%+ limited partners; (4) proof of residential address dated within 90 days (utility bill or bank statement); (5) foreign TINs and a completed bank-provided UBO questionnaire; (6) source of funds/source of wealth declaration for the capital contribution, supported by the contributing partner's personal bank statement or brokerage statement; and (7) a copy of the capital call notice and proof of payment routing from the partner's home-country bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or tiered ownership structure involving a foreign holding company, nominee partners, discretionary trusts, or a non-resident corporate general partner, creating FINTRAC beneficial-ownership ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) a complete organizational chart of the LP, its general partner, and all upper-tier entities; (2) notarized UBO declaration identifying every individual with 25%+ control or ownership; (3) trust deed, shareholders' register, or partnership agreement of each upper-tier entity; (4) Canadian tax counsel opinion letter on beneficial ownership and control under PCMLTFA and Quebec law; (5) sanctions and PEP screening confirmation for all named individuals; and (6) a written business rationale for the tiered structure (e.g., asset protection, US/Canada cross-border tax efficiency).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity or unexpectedly large cross-border inbound wires paid for 3D art services without a documented commercial trail, triggering a risk-inconsistency review for a creative BPO.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) executed Master Service Agreements and Statements of Work with identified game studios, naming the specific game title, asset list, and milestone schedule; (2) itemized invoices matching each wire with unique invoice numbers and project codes; (3) digital asset delivery logs (dropbox or perforce-style acceptance records); (4) the LP's treasury policy letter describing the client payment flow and FX conversion policy; and (5) annual audited or reviewed financial statements if available, plus the LP's T5013 allocations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of PayPal and third-party payment aggregators as primary inbound rails, raising concerns about commingling of business and personal funds, sanctions-adjacent payers, and unreported gross revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) PayPal Business account verification and platform settlement statements matched invoice-by-invoice to the accounting system (Xero/QuickBooks); (2) a signed attestation that no personal PayPal accounts are used for the LP; (3) a reconciliation export showing gross revenue, fees, FX conversion, and net settlement to the Canadian bank account; (4) signed client contracts for each aggregated payment stream; and (5) a written undertaking to migrate all settlements above CAD 10,000 to SWIFT/ACH rails to preserve FINTRAC EFTR compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Vendor counterparties in high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions receiving outbound disbursements for outsourced 3D sculpting or rigging services, triggering sanctions and third-party money laundering concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) subvendor KYC/ADR package per vendor: enterprise registration certificate, government-issued ID of the beneficial recipient, signed service agreement with IP assignment and wage-provision clauses, and bank account ownership confirmation; (2) confirmation through Global Affairs Canada and OSFI sanctions lists that the jurisdiction and counterparty are permitted; (3) a compliance officer sign-off and, where red flags remain, immediate transaction suspension and voluntary FINTRAC disclosure; and (4) a vendor jurisdiction policy restricting payments to FATF-listed high-risk jurisdictions absent express general-partner approval and enhanced monitoring.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for partner capital injections: (1) each non-resident partner remits from its own verified bank account via SWIFT MT103 to the LP's designated CAD operating account at the primary bank; (2) the remittance information field must read: 'Capital contribution to [LP legal name], partner [legal name], dated [date], ref [capital call notice number]'; (3) Canada has no mandatory BOP or purpose-code regime, but the bank's reason-for-payment dropdown should indicate 'other capital investment' or 'capital contribution to limited partnership' where prompted; (4) if funds arrive in USD, a simultaneous spot FX deal ticket must be recorded with the bank at the executed rate; (5) the LP must maintain a partner capital ledger with partner-by-partner lines, the signed capital call notice, the executed partnership agreement, and the bank payment order as AML proof; (6) partner loans used to fund working capital must be supported by a written loan agreement and labeled 'shareholder loan' to prevent recharacterization as a capital contribution or taxable income; (7) where a general partner resolution authorizes the account signatories, a certified copy must be provided to the bank with each new signatory appointment; and (8) all inbound injections exceeding CAD 10,000 will be captured by the bank's FINTRAC EFTR filing, so the LP should pre-emptively provide the source-of-funds package referenced in the KYC defense.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing and settlement for outbound trade payments: (1) primary rail for vendor invoices above CAD 10,000 is a SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) via the LP's Schedule I bank, using beneficiary IBAN/account and SWIFT/BIC, with purpose text 'payment for digital art services under contract no. [x]'; (2) for settlement cover, MT202/COV must be used where required by the correspondent bank; (3) domestic CAD disbursements to Canadian contractors should clear through Payments Canada Lynx (formerly LVTS) for high-value and ACSS for standard EFT or direct deposit; real-time payments may be executed via Interac e-Transfer or the Real-Time Rail (RTR) for low-value urgent amounts; (4) USD disbursements to US-based artists should route via ACH through the bank's cross-border USD platform or via SWIFT for priority, with supplier portal confirmations; (5) a Commercial Letter of Credit is over-engineered for service contracts but a standby LC may be issued where a major studio co-producer requires a bank payment undertaking; (6) PayPal is acceptable only for small-balance (sub-threshold) seed payments to individual freelancers during onboarding of new vendors, with an automatic escalation to SWIFT/ACH once cumulative monthly volume exceeds CAD 10,000; and (7) the LP should record each payment against an AP subledger and preserve the vendor invoice, delivery acceptance, and MT103 confirmation to support the services-vs-royalty characterization and the zero-rating of supplies to non-resident clients.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) executed through the LP's licensed Canadian dealer or the primary bank's FX desk for immediate settlement of receivables and vendor disbursements.

Outright forward foreign exchange contracts (vanilla FX forwards, tenors up to 24 months) for hedging the USD/CAD revenue stream, documented under an ISDA 1992/2002 Master Agreement or a bank FX master agreement with credit support annex and a dedicated treasury line.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for settlement of revenue or vendor payments in restricted or non-deliverable currencies (e.g., KRW, IDR, BRL, CLP) arising from regional gaming clients, executed solely through the bank's NDF desk and limited to bona fide commercial exposure.

Vanilla European-style FX options (plain vanilla puts and calls on CAD/USD or CAD/EUR) used to cap conversion costs on large milestone receipts, purchased or written only for underlying commercial exposure and never on a naked speculative basis, with board/general-partner authorization.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) and cross-currency interest rate swaps for matched asset-liability flows where partner capital is advanced in USD and the LP's revenue is CAD-denominated; requires ISDA/CSA execution, a client swap line, and compliance with hedge-accounting documentation under IFRS 9 so that gains/losses are recognized on income account consistently with the underlying hedged transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) update of limited partnership information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary date of the enterprise's registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100–500; repeated overs2 consecutive years may lead to administrative cancellation (strike-off) of the LP's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (short form) for the Canadian partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal period ending on December 31, file by June 30 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties under Income Tax Act s. 162: $100–$2,500 per year, plus additional penalties for gross negligence or repeated failures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Slips (income and partnership allocation) to all partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the calendar year in which the fiscal period ends
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of $25–$100 per slip (capped), or a higher penalty for fictitious slips.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit assigned to a Quebec limited partnership under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; audit arises only when stipulated in the partnership agreement or required by lenders/investors.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Partnership must maintain books and accounting records in accordance with Canadian ASPE (or IFRS if the LP is a public entity); financial statements are prepared for income tax allocation and partner reporting, but not filed publicly unless requested by CRA.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Limited partnerships are not subject to Quebec's share register UBO filing; instead, the annual declaration filed with the REQ must reflect all current general and limited partners, their addresses, contributions, and any transfers of partnership interests during the year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of capital contributions and profit shares
Minutes of partner meetings and resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 8,000–15,000 (only if a formal audit is contractually required)
